sentences.text: Both the aforesaid appeals have arisen from a common judgment of conviction/sentence passed by the Court of Sessions, Anuppur, in ST/34/2020.

Vide the aforesaid judgment, both the appellants have been convicted and sentenced to undergo R.I. in the following manner :-
 CONVICTION   Section Act Imprisonment Fine if depos  details   365 IPC, 1860 R.I. for 07 years Rs.1000/- 
 
 366 IPC, 1860 R.I. for 10 years Rs.2000/- 
 
 376(D) IPC, 1860 R.I. for life Rs.5,000/-
 
 392 r/w IPC, 1860 R.I. for 10 years Rs.2,000/-
 34
All the sentences have been ordered to run concurrently.
The amount of fine has already been deposited by the appellants.

2. Initially, a missing report was lodged by the husband of the prosecutrix on 12.07.2020, in Police Station Jaithari, District Anuppur, vide which it was alleged that the prosecutrix and the 10 months minor daughter were 2 CRA-838-2024 abducted by the appellants and were taken to some undisclosed place.
The description of the prosecutrix and minor daughter were given.

The victim was recovered on 12.07.2020 and her statement (Exhibit - D/1) was recorded on 13.07.2020,
wherein she had stated that she was in love with Bablu Rathore who had committed bad act with her on many occasions under the pretext of solemnizing marriage with her.

3 . As per the prosecution story, on 11.07.2020, at about 11 am, the prosecutrix along with her mother-in-law Geeta Rathore and minor daughter came to visit Doctor at Lengra in order to get Bablu Rathore vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50223817/
1 treatment for the minor daughter.

sentences.text:
When they reached in front of Municipal Council at about 12 pm,
then a motor cycle came from the front side which was being driven by Bablu Rathore and Nathu Rathore was pillion rider.
Nathu Rathore de-boarded the motor cycle and caught hand of the prosecutrix and forcibly made her to sit on the motor cycle alongwith the minor daughter.
The alarm raised by the prosecutrix did not attract anyone.

At some distance, the friend of Bablu Rathore namely Aniruddh Rathore was found along with his motor cycle at Rathore Chowk and he also accompanied the motor cycle of Bablu Rathore and started going towards Anuppur.
Thereafter, all the three took the prosecutrix on motor cycle towards Anuppur.
The motor cycle was being driven by Nathu Rathore.
Bablu Rathore was sitting at the back of the prosecutrix who was made to sit in the middle.
Bablu Rathore snatched the mangal sutra of the prosecutrix and sent the prosecutrix and her daughter with Aniruddh in order to get the daughter of the prosecutrix medically examined by the Doctor.
Aniruddh took the prosecutrix and her daughter to the clinic of Mr. A.K. Rathore near Tahsil where Nathu Rathore and Bablu Rathore were already present.
Bablu Rathore got his Blood 3 CRA-838-2024 Pressure checked in the clinic.
There was only one boy who was recording the Blood Pressure of Bablu Rathore and the same was not known to the prosecutrix.
Thereafter, Aniruddh took the minor daughter of the prosecutrix and went out along with Nathu Rathore.
Bablu Rathore committed rape upon the prosecutrix in the clinic by alluring her to perform marriage.

Thereafter,
all the three took the prosecutrix to Balbhera at about 5 pm.
Bablu left the prosecutrix at the residence of one Ramkali Rathore with whom he was having acquaintance and thereafter, he went away.
Thereafter, on 12.07.2020 at about 10 am, Bablu took the prosecutrix along with her daughter and left them in the forest of Balbhera and he also left the place.

The prosecutrix by recording the aforesaid statement on 13.07.2020 did not attribute any overt act to Natthulal Rathore and Aniruddh, except Bablu Rathore with whom she was having physical relations for the last three years.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the mother -in-law of the prosecutrix was present along with her at the time when the alleged kidnapping took place on 11.07.2020.
The mother-in-law did not lodge any report on 11.07.2020, rather, the missing report was lodged by the husband of the prosecutrix on 12.07.2020.

The statement of the prosecutrix under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded only on 28.07.2020, wherein the prosecutrix had attributed overt act in terms of offence under Section 376 IPC even qua Nathu and Aniruddh.
The DNA Profile was found to be positive only qua Bablu with whom the prosecutrix was having physical relations for the last three years.
The DNA Profile qua Nathu and Aniruddh was found to be negative.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants further submitted that in view of the aforesaid factual position,
the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. recorded after seven days of the occurrence is nothing but an improvement made by the 4 CRA-838-2024 prosecutrix over and above the original version recorded by her soon after the occurrence on 13.07.2020.
The appellants remained on bail during the pendency of the appeal and now, they are in custody from the date of conviction.
The appellant Bablu is studying in 2nd Semester of L.L.B. in Rewa University.
The appellants crave indulgence of this Court in their first attempt for grant of suspension of sentence.

6. Per contra, learned Government Advocate appearing for the State opposed the prayer for grant of bail on the basis of prosecution story and primarily relied upon the statement of the prosecutrix Bablu Rathore vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50223817/
2 under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and DNA Profile so far as the complicity of Bablu is concerned.

sentences.text:
7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
8.
Admittedly, the prosecutrix is a married woman having two kids.
The manner in which the occurrence had taken place would remain debatable in the context of complicity of the appellants in the commission of offence under Section 376 IPC.

In view of the aforesaid prima-facie consideration of the case, we deem it appropriate to direct the release of the appellants - Nathulal Rathour and Bablu Rathore b y suspending their remaining jail sentence, subject to their executing adequate bail bonds in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- each (Rs. Fifty Thousand Each) with one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Chief Judicial Magistrate concerned with a further direction to appear before the trial Court concerned on 20.09.2024 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard, during the pendency of this appeal.
9 . Accordingly, I.A. No.I.A. No.4670/2024 and I.A. No.7178/2024 are allowed.
5 CRA-838-2024 10. Nothing observed herein above shall be construed to be an opinion on the merits of the case.
